title: setup-proper-dev-environment-with-typescript-ins
description: setup proper dev environment with typescript installed and package.json scripts for building

researchNotes: Changeflow extension currently has package.json with only runtime dependencies typebox and xstate, no scripts, no devDependencies, and no tsconfig.json. package-lock.json mirrors only those runtime deps. This explains why `tsc` is unavailable for local validation.

Pi extension docs say TypeScript extensions are loaded directly by jiti, so a build step is not required for runtime. However npm dependencies next to the extension are resolved normally, and distributed package docs say Pi core packages such as @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent and typebox should be peerDependencies for packages. For this local project extension, devDependencies can provide type checking without changing runtime loading.

Relevant type package for the imported ExtensionAPI/ExtensionContext is @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent. The installed Pi version in the Nix store is 0.70.6 and npm has @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.70.6 available, so the devDependency can be pinned to 0.70.6 to match the current runtime.

Need TypeScript devDependencies: typescript and @types/node for node:fs/node:path declarations. A likely tsconfig should use module/moduleResolution NodeNext, target ES2022, noEmit true, strict true or at least noImplicitAny, skipLibCheck true, and include index.ts.

Pi examples with package.json commonly define scripts clean/build/check, even when build/check are no-ops. For Changeflow, scripts should become useful: e.g. `check`: `tsc --noEmit`, `build`: `tsc --noEmit`, and optionally `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`. Since Pi runs TS directly, build can be a validation alias rather than emitting JS.

Dry-run `npm install --package-lock-only --save-dev typescript @types/node @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.70.6` from pi/extensions/changeflow completed successfully and would update lockfile without installing node_modules; no source files were modified during research.
decisions: Sufficient context exists to plan adding a local TypeScript dev environment: update package.json with build/check/typecheck scripts and devDependencies, add tsconfig.json, refresh package-lock.json, and verify npm run check/build.

Research found that the Changeflow extension needs a local TypeScript dev environment: add tsconfig.json, add build/check/typecheck scripts to package.json, add TypeScript/Node/Pi type devDependencies, refresh package-lock.json, and validate with npm scripts.

Execution order is sequential: create issues.md first, add tsconfig, update package scripts and devDependencies, refresh lockfile/install deps, run validation and fix types, then document dev commands.

Implemented TypeScript dev environment: added issues.md, tsconfig.json, npm build/check/typecheck scripts, TypeScript/Node/Pi devDependencies with refreshed lockfile, documented commands, and fixed surfaced type errors. npm run check and npm run build pass.

QA reran npm run check and npm run build successfully. Reviewed git status and grep output: intended files changed are README, index type fixes, package/package-lock, new issues.md, and new tsconfig.json.
